episodes.186245: A compact but strong upper level trough moved out of New Mexico into the Texas Panhandle on the afternoon of the 30th. Although surface temperatures were relatively cool, modest instability for late November allowed a few isolated thunderstorms to develop. One of these storms produced penny size hail in Kirkland (Childress County).
episodes.186249: A thunderstorm produced a marine thunderstorm wind gust.
episodes.186252: Numerous thunderstorms produced areas of 3 to locally 6 inches of rain...leading to localized flooding.
episodes.186329: A kona low developed west-northwest of the Hawaiian Islands and brought periods of heavy rainfall and isolated thunderstorms. Heavy rainfall lead to localized flash flooding and landslides across portions of the State. Impacts from the kona low continued into December 2023 and are covered in episode 186869.

events.narrative: The Hawaii Police Department reported a landslide closing the Hawaii Belt Rd (Highway 19) between Mile Marker Twelve and Honomu Rd.
A landslide was reported near Mile Marker 28 in Kawaili Gulch along Hawaii Belt rd. (Highway 19).
Roadways flooded between 45th and 39th street. Few high water rescues.
Wind gust was measured at the Galveston Bay WeatherFlow site.
